description: Power-cap packing episodes on the two-site e003 simulator. Every quantity is simulated; every number below is a scenario assumption (nothing is measured data). Power levels, cooling and thermal parameters are read from sim-scenario-v2.json and the measured e002 ratios it points to; the site caps are computed at run time from a commissioning calibration run.
assumptions: Everything here is simulated; no number is a measurement of a real cluster.

Cap: each site cap is its calibrated idle power plus cap.load_fraction of the calibrated idle-to-full-load power span, both measured in the simulator at a constant design outdoor temperature (cap.design_outdoor_c). The design temperature and load fraction are assumptions chosen on calibration and dev seeds, not on test seeds.

Jobs: synthetic queue with a backlog (utilization goal above 1), GPU counts, durations (1.5 to 10 h, log-uniform), checkpoint cadence and value per GPU-hour (USD, no source) are assumptions. All jobs are marked flexible so the packer may hold them; a job is available at its submit time.

Heat wave: each episode draws a heat wave (centre, width, size) added to the sim scenario's diurnal outdoor temperature; episode time 0 is 06:00 local at the first site (start_hour_utc). The event draw rates, precursor probability and ranges are assumptions of the simulation.
Over-cap penalty (USD per kWh above the site cap) is a scenario parameter; the default and the sweep are assumptions.
Planning horizon (3 h in 5-minute steps) and the learned policy's surrogate reward window (3 h) are scenario choices.
Warm-up (first 25 h of each 41 h episode) uses one shared rule for all forecast policies and is excluded from every reported metric; the evaluation window is the last 16 h.

ETS and ARIMA refit once per hour of decisions (forecast_refresh_bins = 12) and serve the 11 decisions in between from the same paths shifted by the elapsed steps, to keep their run time down; every other forecaster is called at every decision.
